It can produce relevance scores for weighted aggregated answers, act as a reranker, and be trained without explicit question-context compatibility labels.

l: sLM, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, opening
s: The relevance estimator is trained on a small language model. This training benefits the small language model fine-tuned with the estimator, while the estimator can also be separated and applied to large language models.

l: LLM, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, opening
s: Large language models can use a relevance estimator trained on a small language model. They can selectively rely on their parametric knowledge when retrieved contexts have low confidence.

l: context, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, opening
s: A retrieved context that is irrelevant to the query can distract the language model and negatively affect answer accuracy. A low-confidence retrieved context set may lead to wrong answers when the model parrots the context.

l: query, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, opening
s: The query is used to assess whether retrieved contexts are relevant and useful for answering. When its retrieved context set is irrelevant, it can be classified as unanswerable.

l: question, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, opening
s: The question is evaluated together with a context to determine whether the context is useful for answering it. The relevance estimator can be trained without explicit labels for question-context compatibility.

l: RE score, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, opening
s: A precise relevance score measures the relative relevance between contexts and a query. Such scores can support weighted aggregated answers, whereas insufficiently precise scores can direct attention to documents less likely to answer the query.

l: confidence, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, opening
s: Context confidence is measured by the relevance estimator to indicate whether a retrieved context set is useful for answering. It can guide the choice between using the retrieved context, classifying the query as unanswerable, and relying on parametric knowledge.

l: decoding strategies, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, opening
s: A decoding strategy can use the confidence of the context set measured by the relevance estimator. It may classify an irrelevant context set as unanswerable or selectively leverage the language model’s parametric knowledge for a low-confidence set.

l: unanswerable set classification, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, opening
s: Unanswerable classification is enabled when the retrieved context set is irrelevant. The text states that this can preserve most accuracy for the answerable set while minimizing negative effects.

l: RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: This unit reviews traditional RAG and introduces RE-RAG, which combines retrieval, generation, and a relevance estimator. Traditional RAG uses a bi-encoder retriever to select contexts and a generator to produce answers, with RAG-sequence marginalizing answer probabilities across contexts. RE-RAG reranks retrieved contexts using a relevance estimator and replaces retriever similarity-based weights with normalized relevance scores. Its joint training uses generator, relevance-estimation, and token losses combined into a total loss.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: Traditional RAG uses a retriever to obtain related contexts and a generator to produce answers from each question-context pair. It marginalizes answer probabilities across contexts using retrieval-based similarity scores.

l: RE-RAG, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: RE-RAG adds a relevance estimator that reranks initially retrieved contexts and supplies more precise relevance scores for answer generation. It replaces similarity-based marginalization weights with normalized relevance-estimator scores and trains the components jointly.

l: retriever, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: The retriever searches an external knowledge base and returns a related context set. It commonly uses a bi-encoder such as DPR and calculates question-context similarity from independently generated embeddings.

l: question, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: The question is encoded by the retriever and concatenated with each context for the generator and relevance estimator. It is used to determine context similarity, relevance, and the generated answer.

l: context, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: A context is retrieved from an external knowledge base and paired with a question. In RE-RAG, contexts are reranked by relevance and only the top-ranked contexts are used before answer generation.

l: generator, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: The generator takes a question and context as input and produces an answer with probability PG(yi,j|qi,cj). During joint training, its answer likelihood also provides a learning signal for the relevance estimator.

l: answer, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: An answer is generated separately for each question-context pair and can then be marginalized across contexts. The training objective uses the ground-truth answer ai and the generator probability for that answer.

l: RAG-sequence, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: RAG-sequence marginalizes the probabilities of answers generated from individual contexts. The unit focuses on it because it achieves higher performance than RAG-token and supports interpretability of answer generation.

l: answer marginalization, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: Answer marginalization aggregates context-specific answer probabilities into a probability for the answer. Traditional RAG weights these probabilities with normalized similarity scores, while RE-RAG weights them with normalized relevance-estimator scores.

l: retriever similarity score, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: The similarity score is computed as the dot product of independently encoded question and context embeddings. It is used for top-k retrieval and, in traditional RAG, for weighting answer marginalization.

l: relevance estimator (RE), RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: The relevance estimator measures the relevance of a question-context pair using a sequence-to-sequence architecture. It generates a classification token, either "true" or "false," and its normalized probability of "true" is converted to a logit for reranking and answer marginalization.

l: document relevance scores, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: The relevance distribution is formed by applying a softmax to the relevance-estimator logits across contexts. RE-RAG uses this distribution, PRE(qi,cj), to weight context-specific generator probabilities.

l: generator probability distribution, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: The generator probability distribution is formed by computing the log-likelihood of the ground-truth answer for each retrieved context and applying a softmax across contexts. QG(qi,cj) represents the relative relevance implied by the generator.

l: Lgen, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: Lgen combines the negative likelihood of the ground-truth answer with the relevance-estimator probability for each question-context pair. It simultaneously trains answer generation and adjusts the probability of generating the relevance classification token.

l: Lre, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: Lre is the KL-divergence between the relevance distribution PRE and the generator-derived distribution QG. It provides a learning signal for training the relevance estimator without labeled question-context relevance data.

l: Ltot, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: Ltot is the joint training objective defined as Lgen plus scaled versions of Lre and Ltok. The scaling factors α1 and α2 balance the effects of the relevance and token losses.

l: joint training, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.3
s: Joint training optimizes the generator and relevance estimator with three losses: Lgen, Lre, and Ltok. Ltok penalizes the relevance estimator for assigning probability to tokens other than "true" and "false."

l: RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: The unit describes experiments evaluating RE-RAG on the Natural Questions and TriviaQA open-domain question-answering datasets. It explains the datasets, context retrieval setup, exact match and additional evaluation metrics, and baseline comparisons involving FiD, FiD-KD, and large language models. RE-RAG uses an extra module to evaluate contexts, selects the top 25 from 100 retrieved contexts for inference, and generally outperforms comparable baselines in the reported results.

l: RE-RAG, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: RE-RAG is evaluated on Natural Questions and TriviaQA using an extra context-evaluation module and 25 contexts at inference. Its reported results generally outperform comparable FiD-KD and other baseline systems, with RE-RAGFlan-large achieving 62.5 F1 on Natural Questions and 78.7 F1 on TriviaQA among the small-generator group.

l: Natural Questions, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: Natural Questions is an open-domain dataset of real questions asked by users on the web, with long-answer contexts and short-answer spans. The experiments use the NQ-open version, which retains questions whose short-answer span is at most five tokens.

l: TriviaQA, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: TriviaQA is an open-domain dataset of question-answer pairs collected from trivia enthusiasts, with questions and answers reviewed by human annotators. The experiments use its unfiltered version.

l: open-domain QA, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: The experiments evaluate models for open-domain question answering on Natural Questions and TriviaQA. Performance is primarily compared using exact match, with F1 and accuracy also reported.

l: FiD, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: FiD is described as a strong question-answering system whose application system outperforms RAG-based systems on the QA task. FiDbase and FiDlarge are included as baselines, using 100 contexts for inference.

l: FiD-KD, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: FiD-KD is used as a baseline and as a retriever for experiments with large language models. Its base and large variants are evaluated with 25 or 100 contexts, while its relevance scores are found to work for reranking but not as well for traditional RAG answer generation.

l: relevance estimator (RE), RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: The relevance evaluator is an extra module that evaluates retrieved contexts and selects the top 25 from the top 100 retrieved contexts for inference. It is used in RE-RAG and with several large language model generators.

l: retriever, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: The retriever supplies the top 20 training contexts and the top 100 development and test contexts for the datasets. FiD-KD retrieval is also compared with the RE approach when applied to large language models.

l: exact match, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: Exact match is the primary evaluation metric. Generated answers are normalized by procedures such as lowercasing, punctuation removal, and article stripping, then marked correct when they exactly match one of the dataset's correct answers.

l: context, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: The dataset contains the top 20 retrieved contexts for training and the top 100 retrieved contexts for development and testing. The experiments train with 20 contexts and use the top 25 contexts selected by the relevance evaluator at inference.

l: generator, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 .. 3.3
s: The model generator is reported separately from the extra module that evaluates contexts. Experiments cover small generators of 2B parameters or fewer and large language model generators of at least 7B parameters, including Llama2, Llama3, ChatGPT, and Codex.

l: RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: This unit evaluates RE-RAG, a retrieval-augmented generation system that uses a relevance estimator (RE) with T5, Flan-T5, and several large language model generators. On Natural Questions (NQ) and TriviaQA (TQA), RE-RAG outperforms traditional RAG with the same total number of parameters and performs competitively with FiD-based models. RE improves context re-ranking and unanswerable set classification compared with FiD-KD and MonoT5 in overall F1 performance. When applied to Llama2, RE also surpasses Self-RAG, while performance on TQA depends more strongly on the generator model.

l: RE-RAG, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: RE-RAG uses a relevance estimator to measure question-context relevance before generation. It achieves higher accuracy than traditional RAG on NQ and TQA with the same total number of parameters and performs competitively with FiD-based models.

l: relevance estimator (RE), RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: The relevance estimator improves the reliability of RAG by more accurately measuring relevance between questions and contexts. It performs strongly as a re-ranker and as a classifier for context sets that lack an answer, and when applied to Llama2 it surpasses Self-RAG.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Traditional RAG is used as the comparison system for RE-RAG. RE-RAG performs better than traditional RAG despite having the same total number of parameters.

l: Natural Questions, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Natural Questions, denoted NQ, is one of the two datasets used to evaluate RE-RAG. RE-RAG performs better on NQ, which the text characterizes as the more knowledge-intensive task.

l: TriviaQA, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: TriviaQA, denoted TQA, is one of the datasets used to evaluate RE-RAG. Its performance appears to depend more on the generator model, and REPLUG with Codex scores slightly higher in TQA.

l: FiD-KD, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: FiD-KD is used as a comparison retriever and as a baseline for re-ranking and unanswerable set classification. RE performs better than FiD-KD on re-ranking recall and F1 classification, although FiD-KD has higher recall for identifying unanswerable context sets.

l: retriever, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: The retriever supplies the top-100 contexts for re-ranking and the top-25 context sets for unanswerable classification. Compared with the relevance estimator, the retriever has higher recall but lower precision and F1 in unanswerable set classification.

l: question-answering performance, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Question-answering performance is evaluated for the complete RAG system on NQ and TQA. RE-RAG improves accuracy over traditional RAG and is competitive with models based on FiD structures, while TQA performance is more dependent on the generator than NQ performance.

l: re-ranking, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: The relevance estimator is evaluated as a re-ranker over the top-100 contexts retrieved by FiD-KD. It achieves higher Recall@1, Recall@5, Recall@10, and Recall@20 than FiD-KD and MonoT5 on both NQ and TQA, with greater efficiency when fewer contexts are used.

l: unanswerable set classification, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Unanswerable set classification identifies top-25 context sets that contain no gold answer. The relevance estimator has higher F1 than FiD-KD and MonoT5 on both NQ and TQA because it provides a better balance between precision and recall, although FiD-KD achieves higher recall.

l: RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: This unit evaluates RE and RE-RAG for handling low-confidence context sets, including when to classify a query as unanswerable or rely on an LLM’s parametric knowledge. The mixed strategy generally improves TriviaQA performance and preserves Natural Questions performance, although gains depend on the availability of parametric knowledge. RE also generalizes better than FiD-KD to unseen datasets, with smaller drops in reranking recall and answer performance. Ablations show that RE’s reranking, relevance scoring, normalization, and generator-informed loss each contribute to performance.

l: RE-RAG, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: RE-RAG combines relevance-estimator reranking and relevance scores in answer generation. Its ablation results show that both improved context selection and improved context weighting contribute to its performance, while the full RE-RAGbase model outperforms the baseline on Natural Questions and TriviaQA.

l: relevance estimator (RE), RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: The relevance estimator ranks contexts, produces relevance scores for answer marginalization, and estimates confidence through the probability of generating the “true” token. On unseen datasets, it shows smaller reranking and answer-performance drops than FiD-KD.

l: FiD-KD, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: FiD-KD experiences larger performance degradation than the relevance estimator when applied to unseen datasets. It also loses more answerable-set accuracy when low-confidence contexts are classified as unanswerable.

l: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: Retrieval-augmented generation uses contextual knowledge retrieved for the query. The analysis finds that small models can use retrieval-augmented generation efficiently when the retrieved context has high confidence, while alternative knowledge sources are useful for low-confidence cases.

l: low-confidence context set, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: A low-confidence context set can trigger either an unanswerable response in a small language model or a switch to parametric knowledge in a large language model. These sets are identified using the confidence score derived from the relevance estimator.

l: confidence score, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: The confidence score is determined by the maximum probability assigned to the “true” token by the relevance estimator for contexts in a set. Thresholds selected for classification performance determine when the model should answer “unanswerable” or use parametric knowledge.

l: parametric knowledge, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: Parametric knowledge is more abundant in large language models and can be used when retrieved contexts have low confidence. Its usefulness varies by dataset: it generally benefits TriviaQA, while its scarcity limits gains on Natural Questions, especially for Llama 2.

l: unanswerable set classification, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: Classifying low-confidence context sets as unanswerable causes only minor answerable-set accuracy loss for the relevance estimator while substantially improving performance on unanswerable sets. The corresponding strategy is less effective with FiD-KD because preserving answerable-set accuracy reduces its unanswerability-classification ability.

l: Natural Questions, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: Natural Questions is evaluated as a more knowledge-intensive dataset than TriviaQA. The mixed strategy usually avoids major losses on it, but parametric knowledge provides less benefit, particularly for Llama 2 models.

l: TriviaQA, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: TriviaQA generally benefits from selectively using parametric knowledge for low-confidence context sets. The mixed strategy improves performance in most of the reported model settings.

l: Llama 3, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: Llama 3 models are evaluated with retrieval-augmented and parametric decoding across model sizes. On TriviaQA, smaller Llama 3 models can approach larger-model accuracy at high confidence, while the gap between model sizes becomes larger at low confidence.

l: LLM, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: LLMs are described as having abundant parametric knowledge that can be directly used when retrieved contexts are unreliable. The largest model within each model family serves as the parametric knowledge base in the mixed strategy.

l: context, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: Context sets are divided into answerable sets, containing at least one gold answer, and unanswerable sets, containing none. Their relevance and confidence affect reranking, answer generation, and the choice between contextual and parametric knowledge.

l: mixed strategy, RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / 5.1 .. 5.3
s: The mixed strategy uses retrieved context when its confidence is high and otherwise bypasses the context in favor of the largest model’s parametric knowledge. It produces gains mainly on TriviaQA, with larger benefits for smaller models when parametric knowledge is effective.

s: Research on Question Answering has improved system performance by using external knowledge and more accurate retrieval methods. Subsequent work improved FiD's structural advantages, while Atlas achieved state-of-the-art performance through a better retriever and increased model scale. s: Question Answering systems can improve their performance by utilizing external knowledge about questions. Research has also studied more accurate retrieval of external knowledge to make these systems more efficient.

s: RAG models have received renewed attention because large language models can directly input context. Recent approaches improve performance by training retrievers that can also be applied to large language models or by reviewing questions and context within the model itself.

s: The RE-RAG framework extends traditional RAG by incorporating an RE module that measures the relative relevance and confidence of contexts. l: Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, Abstract
s: The paper introduces personalized agents powered by large language models that use a user’s smartphone memories to improve downstream applications. It presents EMG-RAG, which combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation with an Editable Memory Graph and uses Reinforcement Learning to address data collection, editability, and selectability. Experiments on a real-world dataset show that EMG-RAG improves performance by approximately 10% over the best existing approach. The personalized agents were also transferred to a real smartphone AI assistant, enhancing usability.

l: Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 1
s: The unit examines personalized agents that use personal memories from smartphones to enhance AI assistants with large language model capabilities. It identifies challenges in collecting, editing, and selectively retrieving personal memories, and proposes EMG-RAG to address them. EMG-RAG uses an Editable Memory Graph for structured memory management and an RL agent for adaptive memory selection. Experiments on a real-world business dataset show improvements in question answering, autofill forms, and user services, and the agents were transferred into an AI assistant product.

l: memories, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 1
s: Personal memories are information generated across smartphone conversations, screenshots, emails, calendars, location histories, travel activities, and other apps. They are organized chronologically and require insertion, deletion, replacement, and selective retrieval because they continuously evolve.

l: personalized agents, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 1
s: AI assistants, including Apple’s Siri, generate or contain users’ personal memories through everyday conversations and apps. The unit studies personalized agents that enhance AI assistants by using these memories with large language models.

l: large language models, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 1
s: Large language models provide semantic understanding and reasoning capabilities for developing personal AI assistants. In the proposed approach, a frozen large language model generates answers from selected memories.

l: EMG-RAG, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 1
s: EMG-RAG is proposed as a solution for the data collection, editability, and selectability challenges of personalized agents. It combines an Editable Memory Graph with retrieval-augmented generation and reinforcement learning for adaptive memory selection.

l: Editable Memory Graph, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 1
s: The Editable Memory Graph is a three-layer data structure for managing personal memories. Its first two layers form a tree organized by business scopes, while its third layer is a user memory graph that captures relationships among memories and supports efficient editing and retrieval within relevant partitions.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 1
s: Retrieval-Augmented Generation is discussed as a way to retrieve relevant memories and provide them as context to a large language model. The unit notes that Needles in a Haystack can introduce context overhead and noise, while advanced approaches often use a fixed Top-K that may miss diverse memory combinations.

l: Reinforcement Learning, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 1
s: Reinforcement learning is used to optimize memory selection end to end. The selected memories prompt a frozen large language model to generate answers, and downstream task quality provides rewards that guide policy improvement.

l: RL agent, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 1
s: The RL agent adaptively selects memories from the Editable Memory Graph without being restricted to a fixed Top-K value. Its selections are evaluated through the quality of answers generated by a frozen large language model.

s: GPT-4 is used to clean raw business data into personal memories and to generate question-and-answer pairs within sessions. The memories involved in generating those pairs are tagged for subsequent training.

s: The business dataset was collected from a real AI assistant and includes daily conversations with the assistant and users’ app screenshots. It is used to extract personal memories and evaluate personalized agents across multiple downstream applications.

l: question answering, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 1
s: Question answering is one of the downstream applications evaluated in the unit. EMG-RAG improves performance by approximately 10.6% over the best existing approach.

s: User services are one of the downstream applications evaluated on the real-world business dataset. EMG-RAG improves performance by approximately 9.7% over the best existing approach.

l: Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 2
s: This unit reviews personalized dialogue systems, retrieval-augmented generation on knowledge graphs, and model editing. It describes how PersonaChat supports research on personalized dialogue, including mutual persona perception, persona sparsity, and long-term persona memory, and how P2BOT enriches dialogue through mutual persona perception. The study constructs user-personalized agents from practical memory data gathered by smartphone AI assistants for question answering, autofill forms, and user services. It also introduces an EMG structure for managing users’ personal memories, applies reinforcement learning to optimize graph-based memory selection, and supports dynamic edits with retrieval-augmented generation using a frozen large language model.

l: Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 3
s: The unit concerns developing personalized agents for users on smartphone AI assistant platforms such as Apple’s Siri and Samsung’s Bixby. These agents are intended to perform personalized tasks while supporting editability, allowing responses to change with users’ dynamic memory data. They must also provide selectability by identifying relevant memories and combining multiple memories through a base language model when needed. The agents support applications including question answering, autofill forms, reminders, and travel navigation.

l: personalized agents, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 3
s: Personalized agents assist users on smartphone AI assistant platforms with personalized tasks. They are designed to support editability and selectability, enabling applications such as question answering, autofill forms, reminders, and travel navigation.

l: Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.4
s: This unit presents EMG-RAG, a framework for personalized agents integrated with smartphone AI assistants. It describes data collection from conversations and screenshots, GPT-4-based memory and question-answer pair generation, and construction of an Editable Memory Graph with hierarchical memory types and entity relationships. An MDP uses reinforcement learning to traverse the graph and select memories for a large language model to answer questions. The unit also discusses question answering, autofill forms, user services, and online learning to address the cold-start problem.

s: The personalized agent is trained from conversations, screenshots, memories, and question-answer pairs to support users through a smartphone AI assistant. It uses retrieved memories to answer questions and provide other services.

s: Data collection involves gathering raw conversations and screenshots, extracting screenshot content with OCR, generating memories, and creating question-answer pairs. GPT-4 is used to reduce manual effort and provide labels for retrieval and generation training.

s: A memory is a key piece of information extracted from raw user data and denoted by M. Memories are organized in the Editable Memory Graph and used as labels and retrieval units for answering questions.

s: Question-answer pairs are generated from several memories and include the memories required to answer each question. They are used to train the memory-selection process and the personalized agent.

s: Editable Memory Graph construction uses four predefined memory types, Relationship, Preference, Event, and Attribute, and subclass partitions. Entity recognition creates nodes, relation extraction creates edges, and TransE embeddings connect entities with nearby subclasses.

s: The memory graph represents entities as nodes and their relationships as edges, with each in-degree node associated with one or more memories. Its structure allows traversal across different memory subclasses and supports efficient retrieval.
